KMS/HSM key rotation and envelope encryption
Telemetry pruning policies and ejection rules
Dedicated vs Hosted cost tradeoffs and throughput expectation
meeting_header: Date: 2026-11-18 | Time: 15:00 PST | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (Sunridge), Tom Bauer (Sunridge), Rita Lopez (Sunridge)
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you carving time. I'm Lena, I'm the account lead on this. Marco from our SE team will walk through the console and some API flows for your telemetry and retention needs.
[00:07] Aisha Khan: Great thanks. We are looking for a quick tour, high level first then dive on PII redaction, key mgr, and ephemeral modes. Tom, you and I will focus on security bits.
[00:15] Marco Diaz: Cool. Quick agenda — show Console toggles, show API flags, then a few Optimize recommendations for batching and KV caching that reduce cost while keeping latency.
[00:22] Rita Lopez: On the timeline, we want to see a POC in early December. Budget is a soft constraint but security and legal are blockers first.
[00:30] Marco Diaz: Understood. Jumping into the Console — this is the request-storage panel, note we have three modes: stored (default), ephemeral, and ejected. The ephemeral mode drops requests after inference and only preserves minimal telemetry by default.
[00:45] Tom Bauer: When you say minimal telemetry, what fields remain? We need to know what is still going to logs for our SIEM.
[00:53] Marco Diaz: Good question. Minimal telemetry includes routing meta, timing, and token counts. We can strip out request payloads entirely via the redaction rules. There's a toggle for 'payload retention' and then granular redaction rules where you can drop patterns, regexes, or structured fields.
[01:06] Aisha Khan: Regex rules — can we import a set? Our platform uses a consistent meta key names, would rather not recreate all rules manually.
[01:12] Marco Diaz: Yep, you can upload a JSON ruleset or use our UI to paste patterns. We'll send a sample template. The patch supports named groups so you can map PII types.
[01:25] Lena Park: One clarification — for ephemeral mode, you mentioned KV cache interaction earlier in the doc. How does ephemeral work with prefix caching for repeated prompts?
[01:34] Marco Diaz: Right. Ephemeral storage applies to request/response logs; the KV cache for inference is independent and held in GPU memory per session. You can enable prefix caching without persisting request bodies. That keeps latency benefits but avoids storing raw prompts.
[01:48] Tom Bauer: Encryption at rest — if for some reason we pick stored mode for a subset, can we bring our own KMS keys?
[01:54] Marco Diaz: Yes, BYOK is supported; our Private deployment also supports HSM integrations. For Hosted we have KMS hooks and envelope encryption. Your rotation policies are honored, and we keep audit records for key operations.
[02:07] Rita Lopez: How about exports for audit? We need an immutable trail for legal review.
[02:11] Marco Diaz: Exportable audit logs are available; retention windows are configurable per route. We can show you the audit export flow — it's available via Console and API.
[02:20] Lena Park: Let's demo a concrete flow — Marco, can you simulate sending a request with sensitive fields and show the redaction live?
[02:27] Marco Diaz: Sure, switching screens. I'm going to send a sample payload containing a name, SSN-like number, and a credit account number. Watch the logs.
[02:35] [02:35] Marco Diaz (screen): POST /v1/generate payload {name: "Alice Morris", ssn: "123-45-6789", amount: "$3,200.00"}
[02:48] Marco Diaz: Console shows raw capture on the left; redaction pipeline is applied before storage. Here I add a rule: regex "\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b" -> mask.
[03:01] Rita Lopez: Looks like the stored body now has masked ssn and account digits redacted — good.
[03:08] Tom Bauer: Is the masking reversible by admins? We need to ensure masking is one-way for compliance.
[03:13] Marco Diaz: Masking as shown is irreversible; we also offer tokenization + envelope encryption if you need reversible with strict access controls, but that implies a key escrow model.
[03:24] Aisha Khan: So if we tokenized certain fields we could store token mappings in our own vault?
[03:28] Marco Diaz: Exactly. You can integrate with your KMS and vault to hold token mappings. Redwood's audit logs will show token access events.
[03:38] [03:38] Lena Park: Aisha — do you expect most traffic to be ephemeral or stored for Sunridge?
[03:42] Aisha Khan: Likely ephemeral for customer-identifying flows, stored for aggregated analytics and ops. We want selective retention per route or per model.
[03:51] Marco Diaz: You can scope retention policies per route, per model and even per customer ID. The 'prune' policy can be schedule-based or event-triggered.
[03:59] Rita Lopez: Event-triggered pruning — give an example?
[04:02] Marco Diaz: For example, if a message is flagged by your internal DLP or matches a high-risk pattern, you can trigger automatic ejection of that request and its descendants via a webhook.
[04:13] Tom Bauer: Webhook — how do we secure that? Mutual TLS?
[04:16] Marco Diaz: We support mTLS and HMAC signatures for webhook authenticity.
[04:21] [04:21] Aisha Khan: On the API surface, is there a simple flag to say ephemeral=true per request? We have multiple services calling the API so per-request control would be ideal.
[04:30] Marco Diaz: Yes, there's a request header and an SDK arg. Header X-Redwood-Request-Mode: ephemeral | stored. If ephemeral is set, the system honors the policy chain and avoids writing request bodies.
[04:43] Rita Lopez: What about partial retention — mask some fields and keep the rest?
[04:47] Marco Diaz: Supported. You can apply field-level scrubbing using JSON path rules and keep non-sensitive fields.
[04:54] Lena Park: Cost impact — ephemeral reduces storage, but does it affect per-token charge?
[05:00] Marco Diaz: Storage-related charges go down but inference compute is the same. There are features in Optimize that recommend batching, KV cache settings, and quantization for workloads that have high token per request. That can lower per-token effective cost.
[05:12] Aisha Khan: We have two classes: low-latency customer-facing chat and high-throughput batch scoring. For chat we care about latency; for batch scoring we care cost. Can Redwood route to different model variants automatically?
[05:24] Marco Diaz: Yes — smart routing by route or header. You can pin a route to a low-latency variant and a cost-optimized variant for background jobs with automatic fallbacks.
[05:33] Tom Bauer: For the POC we want to exercise the audit export and the pruning webhook. Also need a demo of the BYOK flow.
[05:40] Marco Diaz: Makes sense. I'll include endpoint examples in the sample config and a step-by-step for KMS binding.
[05:46] Lena Park: Quick detour — any regulatory items for EU data residency?
[05:49] Marco Diaz: We support region routing. If you need EU-only storage, routes can be pinned to eu-west and storage can be restricted to that region.
[05:57] Rita Lopez: Can we test a scenario where a user requests ejection mid-session? Like a user-initiated data deletion that triggers pruning?
[06:03] Marco Diaz: There's a programmatic deletion API and also a subject access endpoint you can call. We can chain that to prune associated KV caches for long-running sessions.
[06:13] Aisha Khan: Ok great. Could you show the logs for a pruned request?
[06:17] Marco Diaz: Switch back to log viewer — here's a request flagged, then an event shows 'prune: true' and the stored content is replaced with a digest and a reason code. The audit log records who triggered the prune and a timestamp.
[06:32] Tom Bauer: Do we get a webhook on prune completion so our systems can reconcile?
[06:36] Marco Diaz: Yes, prune-complete webhooks are available. They include a status and digest to match earlier ephemeral references.
[06:44] Rita Lopez: About rollouts — if we start Hosted and then go Dedicated, how smooth is migration?
[06:49] Marco Diaz: We provide migration tooling; the same API surface is preserved. You'll want to rebind KMS keys in Dedicated and reconfigure region pins, but the client SDKs stay the same.
[06:59] Aisha Khan: On data retention default policies, does Redwood provide SLOs for ejection time? E.g., how quickly is data pruned after trigger?
[07:05] Marco Diaz: For Hosted, typical ejection completes within minutes; Dedicated has SLA options for faster ejection. We can commit to a target in the contract.
[07:13] Lena Park: I'm seeing a couple of hand raises — Rita, Tom any other immediate blockers?
[07:17] Rita Lopez: We need to know whether redaction rules are applied pre or post-indexing for search/analytics.
[07:21] Marco Diaz: Pre-indexing — redaction runs before any downstream indexing or analytics pipelines. You can configure to store sanitized versions for analytics separately.
[07:30] Tom Bauer: Testing harness — can we run a synthetic workload through Optimize recommendations to compare cost?
[07:35] Marco Diaz: Yes, Optimize has a sandbox where you can simulate different batching and quantization parameters against a sample traffic trace. We'll share the simulation link.
[07:44] Aisha Khan: About monitoring — do we get token-level telemetry per route? We need it to feed our chargeback systems.
[07:50] Marco Diaz: Token-level breakdown is available in the Console and via the usage API. You can export per-user or per-route token counts.
[07:57] Lena Park: Great. Wrapping up we'll summarize next steps. But Marco — any gotchas you want to call out?
[08:03] Marco Diaz: Two practical notes: 1) If you rely heavily on prefix caching and ephemeral mode, ensure the cache keys don't include PII fields you intend to prune. 2) Tokenization/reversible schemes require careful KMS/access design — treat them as separate project tracks.
[08:20] Rita Lopez: Noted. Also, for the POC can you scope Dedicated vs Hosted cost difference for our 2M req/day baseline?
[08:27] Lena Park: I'll include ballpark numbers and margin assumptions in the pricing overlay.
[08:31] Aisha Khan: One more question — SSO/SCIM integration for RBAC?
[08:35] Marco Diaz: Full SSO + SCIM for provisioning and role mapping. You can restrict access to the prune API to certain roles.
[08:43] Tom Bauer: Ok, I'll send a short email with our compliance team's contacts and requirements.
[08:47] Lena Park: Perfect — we'll follow up with the doc links and the sample configs. Any last comments?
[08:52] Rita Lopez: No, thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[08:54] Marco Diaz: Thanks — look out for the sample ruleset and the webhook examples.
[08:58] Lena Park: End recap: Marco to provide sample config + prune webhook examples, Lena to send pricing and SOC2/KMS docs, Aisha to share compliance stakeholders. POC kickoff tentatively week of Dec 1.
[09:14] [post-call] Lena Park (chat): dropping link to SOC 2 security pack and sample ruleset - will email full spreadsheet.
